local_facts.claim: Arkansas Code § 16-64-122 compares a claimant's fault with the fault of the party or parties from whom damages are sought. A claimant whose fault is less may recover damages reduced in proportion to that fault; a claimant whose fault is equal to or greater may not recover.
local_facts.why_it_matters: Responsibility needs to be investigated early. In a Jonesboro injury claim, photographs, witness information, reports, visibility conditions, and the complete sequence of events may affect both whether there is a claim and how damages are evaluated.
local_facts.title: Arkansas has a 50-percent comparative-fault bar

local_facts.claim: Craighead County Circuit Court operates from a Western District location at 511 South Main Street in Jonesboro and an Eastern District courthouse at 107 Cobean Boulevard in Lake City.
local_facts.why_it_matters: The right civil filing location depends on the facts and venue rules, not simply the nearest courthouse. Accurate incident locations, addresses, and party information help determine where a Craighead County matter belongs.
local_facts.title: Craighead County has two circuit-court districts

local_facts.claim: UAMS Family Medical Center in Jonesboro states that it serves an 11-county region that includes Craighead and surrounding Northeast Arkansas counties.
local_facts.why_it_matters: Care after an injury may involve facilities and providers beyond the county where the incident occurred. Listing every provider, treatment date, and record location keeps a claim timeline complete.
local_facts.title: Jonesboro care often reaches beyond Craighead County

anchors.label: Ceiling on an injury contingency percentage
anchors.detail: The rule requires only that a fee be reasonable, and gives eight factors for measuring that. No Arkansas statute assigns a percentage to a negligence recovery.

anchors.label: Opening a civil case, Craighead County Circuit Clerk
anchors.detail: The clerk's published amount for initiating a cause of action including the initial summons, built on the $150.00 statutory base. The county's own fee page lists $165.00 for the same line.
anchors.source_name: Craighead County Circuit Clerk filing fees

anchors.label: Legislated limit on an injury or death recovery
anchors.detail: Article 5 says that apart from workers' compensation, no law shall be enacted limiting the amount to be recovered for injuries resulting in death or for injuries to persons or property.

anchors.label: The only Arkansas fee percentage, and it is workers' compensation
anchors.detail: Valid only with Workers' Compensation Commission approval, and on a controverted claim the carrier pays half of it on top of the benefits while the claimant pays the other half.

fee_rows.stage: Share of a Jonesboro injury recovery
fee_rows.note: The eight factors weigh time and labor, difficulty, the fee customarily charged locally, the amount involved and results obtained, the length of the relationship, and whether payment is contingent.

fee_rows.stage: Any engagement likely to produce a fee above this
fee_rows.note: Above that figure the agreement must be confirmed in writing and must state the method by which sums due to the lawyer will be calculated.
It states the percentages accruing on settlement, trial and appeal, the expenses deducted, whether that happens before or after the fee, and a closing written statement follows.

fee_rows.stage: Compensation appeal fees, a separate system
fee_rows.note: Five hundred dollars on appeal to the full Commission and one thousand on appeal to the Court of Appeals or Supreme Court, with a $200 change-of-physician fee alongside.

fee_rows.stage: Sheriff serving a summons or subpoena
fee_rows.note: Charged for every person named unless several are served at one location, with $20.00 to return the paper and $100.00 for a writ of execution.

fee_rows.stage: Reopening a closed circuit court case
fee_rows.note: Set statewide by statute, matching the transfer fee, and the county government page lists the same amount for a reopening.
